terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: The screenshot is a defect reference rather than an ideal rock photo. It clearly proves the current six-to-eight-sided topology and flat face bands are unacceptable. Hidden sides may be inferred procedurally because the scatter is static and non-hero.

reasoning: The dominant close rock occupies hundreds of pixels, so its radial polygon sides and per-face shading are immediately legible.
The system repeats roughly 1600 rubble stones and 1500 pebbles, so topology must scale by projected importance rather than giving every instance hero density.
The desired surface is a continuous worn mass with a few intentional shoulder and crown breaks, not a uniformly faceted assembled solid.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth is required because the individual object is simple but close-range silhouette quality, repeated multi-resolution variants, slope seating, and material breakup all affect the result.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: The dominant rock must have a continuously curved, asymmetrical outline without six-to-eight readable radial sides.
A broad worn shoulder should transition gradually into the upper crown instead of forming one horizontal polygon band.
The crown needs a few localized chips and an off-center high point, not a pyramidal tip.
The base must remain partially buried with a narrow cavity-darkened dust band rather than a floating black wedge.
Subtle warm/cool color variation must break up large surfaces without recreating per-triangle color blocks.
Nearby pebbles need rounded compressed silhouettes with enough segments to avoid pentagonal outlines.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the screenshot viewpoint, no near-field rock exposes a readable radial polygon count or broad flat-shaded face bands.
Large stones select high-detail continuous-sculpt variants; medium rubble and pebbles retain cheaper variants within eight fixed InstancedMesh shape draws.
Stone silhouettes remain asymmetric and weathered, with worn shoulders, off-center crowns, localized chips, and embedded ground contact.
The merged scene retains the existing scatter counts, deterministic placement, slope alignment, collision exclusions, and production frame-rate target.

featureGroups.name: Continuous near-field stone silhouette
qualityCriteria: Near-field rock outlines use enough angular samples that individual radial sides are not readable at the screenshot scale.
The profile remains irregular and eroded rather than becoming a perfect ellipsoid.
failureModes: large rock reads as a cone, pyramid, or stretched primitive

featureGroups.name: Eroded shoulder and crown structure
qualityCriteria: Vertical profile contains enough smoothly varying rings to form a worn lower body, shoulder, crown, and embedded base.
Localized crown chips do not create a global low-poly appearance.
failureModes: one horizontal shoulder band dominates the body
top converges to a pyramidal point

featureGroups.name: Detail-scaled batching
qualityCriteria: Large rubble selects higher radial/ring density variants while ordinary rubble and pebbles use medium-density continuous variants.
Rubble and gravel remain eight fixed InstancedMesh variant draws instead of thousands of WebGPU BatchedMesh sub-draws.
failureModes: every tiny stone pays the hero topology cost
variant quality is random rather than correlated with physical size
draw calls increase with silhouette quality

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

mustMatch: continuous near-field rock silhouettes with no readable radial polygon count
smooth shared-normal shading without broad face bands
worn shoulder, off-center crown, localized chips, and embedded base
eight fixed scatter shape draws and 60 fps production target
niceToHave: subtle crown wear and cavity dust

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Weathered shoulder, crown, and embedded base
Smooth normal continuity and subtle stone variation

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: The source is a screenshot of the current render and is valid geometry-defect evidence, but it is not independent real-world PBR evidence.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Hidden-side erosion may be inferred deterministically because these are static environmental props.
The screenshot is authoritative for the low-poly failure but not for real-world PBR recovery.

componentTree.name: Static stone scatter container
componentTree.topologyRationale: This component is the runtime container for two discrete repeated stone batches, not a visible stone surface.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: five InstancedMesh rubble variants and three InstancedMesh gravel variants
deformationStack: deterministic instance scale, slope alignment, and local-up rotation
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: shared smooth vertex normals on each stored stone variant

localFeatures.geometryEffect: deterministic rounded, slabby, shouldered, and crown-chipped stored geometries

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: smooth shared normals plus deterministic multi-frequency radial displacement
surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: buried base and cavity-biased lower color

componentTree.name: Near-field weathered rock body
componentTree.topologyRationale: The screenshot shows a single worn stone mass whose silhouette should vary continuously; countable planar sides are the reported defect.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: 18-24 angular samples for regular rubble and 30-34 for rare large rubble, with 7-9 vertical profile rings
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: indexed shared vertices with computeVertexNormals and no flatShading

localFeatures.geometryEffect: minimum 18 radial samples with continuous noise instead of independent per-vertex hash jumps
one or two narrow angular depressions confined to the upper rings

surfaceDetail.displacementPattern: continuous angular sine field with vertical phase drift
surfaceDetail.notes: No broad triangle-sized albedo or normal discontinuities.

componentTree.name: Worn shoulder and crown profile
componentTree.topologyRationale: The lower body, shoulder, and crown are continuous parts of the same eroded stone and require multiple smooth profile transitions.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: 7-9 vertically interpolated rings with gradually changing radius and center offset
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: shared smooth normals across adjacent rings

localFeatures.geometryEffect: two intermediate transition rings prevent one dominant horizontal facet band

componentTree.name: Buried stone base
componentTree.topologyRationale: The visible base is a rounded stone volume partially embedded in sand, not a separate hard-edged plinth.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: wider lower rings placed below grade
deformationStack: burial depth proportional to instance height
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: smooth normals with contact darkening in vertex color

localFeatures.geometryEffect: lower 25-35 percent buried below analytic terrain height

componentTree.name: Size-aware rubble and pebble variants
componentTree.topologyRationale: The scatter is an assembly of discrete stone bodies stored once and repeatedly transformed by a fixed set of InstancedMesh groups.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: five rubble geometries and four pebble geometries selected by physical size

localFeatures.geometryEffect: 12-16 radial samples and 5-6 rings for nearby compressed pebbles

materials.name: Weathered high-desert stone

albedo.samplingNotes: Warm sandstone, cooler gray volcanic variants, and lighter worn crowns.

colorVariation.pattern: continuous height and angular mottling stored in vertex color

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: Vertex-frequency bands remain tied to the stored geometry so instance scaling does not create triangle-sized color blocks.

roughness.localResponse: rougher embedded cavities and slightly smoother worn crowns

lightingFromPhoto: Key light: existing warm directional sun from upper left; retain current shadow softness so curvature is legible.
Fill light: existing cool sky/hemisphere fill prevents lower stone faces from collapsing to black.
Rim or environment light: pale desert sky contribution separates the crown silhouette from the ground and horizon.
Exposure and tone mapping: retain the production ACES/filmic exposure target; contact shadow and ambient occlusion remain confined to the buried base.
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Treat the screenshot as geometry-defect evidence, not as independent PBR source pixels.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Uniformly increasing all instances to hero density could waste triangles; selection must correlate with physical size.
Over-smoothing can create plastic ellipsoids; retain low-amplitude continuous erosion and sparse localized chips.
